questions.question: If two lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 are PARALLEL but not coincident, then
questions.explanation: Same slopes (parallel) but different intercepts ⇒ inconsistent (no solution).

questions.question: Solve: x + y = 5, x − y = 1.
Solve: 2x + 3y = 12, 3x − y = 7.
questions.explanation: From 2nd: y = 3x − 7. Sub into 1st: 2x + 3(3x − 7) = 12 ⇒ 11x = 33 ⇒ x = 3, y = 2.

questions.explanation: Let son = s. Father = 4s. After 10 yrs: 4s + 10 = 2(s + 10) ⇒ 4s + 10 = 2s + 20 ⇒ 2s = 10 ⇒ s = 5.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A shopkeeper sells pens at ₹x each. A customer buys 5 pens and pays ₹10 extra for packing, totalling ₹85.

(i) Write a linear equation in x.
(ii) Solve for x.
(iii) What does x represent in this context?
(iv) How much would 8 pens (with the same ₹10 packing) cost?

Read the passage and answer the questions.

In a quiz, each correct answer earns +3 marks and each wrong answer −1 mark. A student attempts 20 questions and scores 32.

(i) Let correct = c, wrong = w. Write two equations.
(ii) Solve them.
(iii) State the number of correct and wrong answers.
(iv) What is the maximum possible score in this quiz?
questions.answer:
(i) c + w = 20 and 3c − w = 32.
(ii) Add: 4c = 52 ⇒ c = 13. Then w = 7.
(iii) Correct: 13. Wrong: 7.
(iv) If all 20 correct: 3·20 = 60 marks.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Given the pair: 2x + 3y = 12 and 4x + 6y = 24.

(i) Compare ratios a₁/a₂, b₁/b₂, c₁/c₂.
(ii) Classify the system (consistent / inconsistent / dependent).
(iii) How many solutions does it have?
(iv) Give any two solutions.
questions.answer:
(i) a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2. b₁/b₂ = 3/6 = 1/2. c₁/c₂ = 12/24 = 1/2. All equal.
(ii) Dependent / coincident lines. The second is just twice the first.
(iii) Infinitely many.
(iv) E.g. (0, 4) — check: 2·0 + 3·4 = 12 ✓. And (6, 0) — check: 12 ✓. Any (x, (12−2x)/3) works.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Two digits of a two-digit number reversed give a number 27 less than the original. The sum of the digits is 11.

(i) Let tens digit = a, units = b. Write the original number and the reversed number.
(ii) Form two equations.
(iii) Solve them.
(iv) State the two-digit number.
questions.answer:
(i) Original = 10a + b. Reversed = 10b + a.
(ii) 10a + b − (10b + a) = 27 ⇒ 9a − 9b = 27 ⇒ a − b = 3. Also a + b = 11.
(iii) Add: 2a = 14 ⇒ a = 7. b = 4.
(iv) The number is 74. (Reversed: 47. 74 − 47 = 27 ✓.)

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A boat travels 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours; and 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream in 13 hours.

(i) Let speed of boat in still water = b km/h and stream = s km/h. Express upstream / downstream speeds.
(ii) Set up two equations using time = distance / speed.
(iii) Use the substitution u = 1/(b − s), v = 1/(b + s) to linearise. Solve for u, v.
(iv) Hence find b and s.
questions.answer:
(i) Upstream speed = b − s; downstream = b + s.
(ii) 30/(b − s) + 44/(b + s) = 10 and 40/(b − s) + 55/(b + s) = 13.
(iii) Let u = 1/(b − s), v = 1/(b + s): 30u + 44v = 10 and 40u + 55v = 13. Multiply first by 4 and second by 3: 120u + 176v = 40, 120u + 165v = 39. Subtract: 11v = 1 ⇒ v = 1/11. Then 30u + 44/11 = 10 ⇒ 30u = 6 ⇒ u = 1/5.
(iv) b − s = 1/u = 5; b + s = 1/v = 11. Add: 2b = 16 ⇒ b = 8. s = 3. Boat 8 km/h, stream 3 km/h.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

The ages of Anu and Banu are in the ratio 5:7. Four years later, their ages will be in the ratio 3:4.

(i) Let Anu's age = 5k, Banu's = 7k. Write the future-age equation.
(ii) Simplify into a linear equation.
(iii) Solve for k.
(iv) State their present ages.
questions.answer:
(i) (5k + 4)/(7k + 4) = 3/4.
(ii) Cross-multiply: 4(5k + 4) = 3(7k + 4) ⇒ 20k + 16 = 21k + 12 ⇒ k = 4.
(iii) k = 4.
(iv) Anu = 20 years, Banu = 28 years. (Verify: 5/7 ✓. After 4 yrs: 24/32 = 3/4 ✓.)

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

The equations 2x + 3y = 10 and 4x + 6y = 25 form a pair.

(i) Check the ratios of coefficients.
(ii) Are the lines parallel? Coincident? Intersecting?
(iii) How many solutions does the system have?
(iv) Is the system consistent?
questions.answer:
(i) a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2; b₁/b₂ = 3/6 = 1/2; c₁/c₂ = 10/25 = 2/5.
(ii) a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ — parallel but not coincident.
(iii) Zero solutions.
(iv) Inconsistent.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

Use the graphical method conceptually for: x + y = 6 and x − y = 2.

(i) Find two points on the first line.
(ii) Find two points on the second.
(iii) Describe (in words) what the lines' intersection means.
(iv) Solve algebraically to confirm the intersection point.
questions.answer:
(i) x + y = 6. Points: (0, 6) and (6, 0).
(ii) x − y = 2. Points: (0, −2) and (2, 0).
(iii) The intersection (x, y) is the unique pair satisfying both equations — graphically, where the two lines cross.
(iv) Add the equations: 2x = 8 ⇒ x = 4. Then y = 2. Intersection at (4, 2).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A word problem: 'Two numbers differ by 5 and their sum is 25.' Solve using two different methods.

(i) Method 1: form two equations and use substitution.
(ii) Method 2: form two equations and use elimination (add/subtract).
(iii) Which method was easier for this problem?
(iv) State the two numbers.
questions.answer:
(i) Let numbers = x, y. x − y = 5 and x + y = 25. From first: x = y + 5. Substitute: (y + 5) + y = 25 ⇒ 2y = 20 ⇒ y = 10, x = 15.
(ii) Add the two equations: 2x = 30 ⇒ x = 15. y = 10.
(iii) Elimination — adding eliminates y in one step. Substitution is also fine but takes more algebra.
(iv) The numbers are 10 and 15.
